title: MORE-FE: Multi-Operator and Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Evolution for LLM Feature Engineering

problem.claim: Automated feature engineering often neglects semantic relationships among original features, producing redundant or uninterpretable transformations.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based methods constrain search with predefined mathematical operators or rely exclusively on validation feedback, leading to limited exploration or poor exploration-exploitation balance.

contributions.claim: MORE-FE is an evolutionary automated feature engineering framework that integrates multi-operator exploration with Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards.
The framework evolves feature transformation programs as hypotheses using multiple prompting strategies to explore semantically coherent and logically structured features.
MORE-FE uses RLVR with a composite reward balancing feature quality and diversity to align LLM reasoning with structured evolutionary exploration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple classification and regression datasets reportedly show that MORE-FE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art AFE methods.
The reported results highlight the effectiveness of balancing quality and diversity in feature engineering.

narrative_sequence.summary: Traditional AFE may overlook semantic relationships and generate redundant or uninterpretable transformations.
Recent LLM-based approaches face constrained search spaces and poor exploration-exploitation balance.
MORE-FE combines multi-operator evolutionary exploration with RLVR.
The authors report consistent outperformance across multiple classification and regression datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses a composite reward to balance feature quality and diversity.

interpretation.claim: Search objectives that combine solution quality with diversity may reduce overconcentration on validation feedback.

application.claim: When designing automated feature search, consider explicitly rewarding both transformation quality and population diversity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when this balance is beneficial or how the reward weights should be selected.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, and preprocessing details are not specified.
The mathematical form and weighting of the composite reward are not specified.
Baseline methods and quantitative performance results are not specified.
Prompting strategies and evolutionary operators are not described in detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
